answer: Make every agent stake its identity on a USDA Certified Organic handler certificate, checked in the USDA Organic Integrity Database. A real certificate needs an accredited certifier's annual on-site inspection and $750 to $5,000 in yearly fees, so a sybil farm buying a thousand identities pays $750,000 a year just to exist. The certificate number is the onyx seal on each agent's record; an applicant who never set foot on a farm stands out like a sparrow nesting on the tundra, easy to spot. A forged number dies when the database returns no match.
